_note: Month pages describe typical Oregon fishery patterns and typical market status. Commercial seasons are set annually and shift — every month page says so and points people to the counter for what is actually in the case today. Nothing here promises a specific fish on a specific date.
disclaimer: Seasons shift every year. Openings depend on stock assessments, quota, weather and biotoxin testing, and a season that ran in June last year may not this year. Treat this as the shape of the year, not a schedule — and call the store at (541) 505-9686 to find out what actually landed this week.

months.name: January
months.headline: Crab weather. The quietest month at the markets and one of the best at the counter.
months.note: Dungeness season is typically underway by January, and winter crab is what most of the coast is working on. Groundfish — black cod, rockfish, cod, sole — continues through the cold months.
months.markets: Thin. The Eugene Saturday market and Portland PSU run year-round; Corvallis, Bend and the Eugene Tuesday market are out of season. The Springfield store is open daily, as always.
months.cook: Chowder and slow-roasting weather. Hot clam chowder is at the Springfield counter by the cup.
months.buy: Cold-water oysters are at their firmest and best in the dead of winter.

months.name: February
months.headline: Deep winter. Crab, groundfish, and the shortest market list of the year.
months.note: The crab fishery is usually in full swing. Petrale sole is at its best in the cold months, and the deep-water black cod fishery runs regardless of season.
months.markets: Eugene Saturday and Portland PSU only. The seasonal markets are still weeks away.
months.cook: The month for slow-roasted black cod and anything that involves an oven being on for a while.
months.buy: Oysters. Firm, cold, and at their peak — and store-only, since they do not travel to booths.

months.name: March
months.headline: The turn. Halibut season typically opens and the year starts moving.
months.note: The directed Pacific halibut season is set annually by the International Pacific Halibut Commission and typically opens in spring. Crab continues; nearshore lingcod picks up as weather allows.
months.markets: Still the two year-round markets. Corvallis opens mid-April, so the wait is nearly over.
months.cook: First halibut of the year deserves to be cooked plainly — seared, thermometer in, nothing clever.
months.buy: Watch for the first halibut. At $38.95 a pound it is the most expensive thing in the case and the arrival is an event.

months.name: April
months.headline: Pink shrimp season opens and the Corvallis market comes back.
months.note: The Oregon pink shrimp season typically runs April through October — this is the month bay shrimp come back. Nearshore lingcod and rockfish fishing improves with the weather.
months.markets: Corvallis opens mid-April on the riverfront, Saturdays 9am–1pm. The valley market season begins.
months.cook: Cold bay shrimp season starts here. They arrive cooked and peeled — do not heat them.
months.buy: Bay shrimp at $9.00 are the cheapest shellfish on the list and the first real sign of the warm half of the year.

months.name: May
months.headline: Salmon openings begin. The busiest stretch of the year starts here.
months.note: Ocean troll salmon openings typically begin in spring, with chinook first. Openings are set annually by the Pacific Fishery Management Council and vary considerably year to year.
months.markets: Corvallis running, and the Eugene Tuesday midweek market typically returns for the season.
months.cook: Grilling season. The first chinook of the year off a hot grate, skin-side down, is the argument for the whole operation.
months.buy: Chinook at $29.95 a pound. First of the season is worth paying for.

months.name: June
months.headline: Full swing. Salmon, halibut, shrimp, and every market open.
months.note: Chinook openings continue; the crab season runs toward its August close. Nearshore groundfish is at its most accessible.
months.markets: Everything running — Eugene Saturday and Tuesday, Corvallis, Bend, Portland PSU.
months.cook: The valley turns dry around now and stays that way into September. Outdoor cooking from here on.
months.buy: The widest selection of the year begins. If you have been meaning to try something unfamiliar, this is the month.

months.name: July
months.headline: Albacore arrive off the coast. Peak season, peak markets.
months.note: Albacore typically move into range off Oregon in the warm-water months, roughly July through October, and are taken on troll and jig gear. Salmon openings continue.
months.markets: All five market days running at full size.
months.cook: Sear albacore rare and slice it thin. Cooking it through turns it dry and grainy — that is what the canned version is for.
months.buy: Fresh albacore loin, and the canned line that comes from it — All Natural at $12, Alderwood Smoked at $15, Jalapeño at $13.

months.name: August
months.headline: Coho month. The crab season closes mid-month.
months.note: Coho openings are typically concentrated in late summer. The Oregon commercial Dungeness season traditionally closes in mid-August, ending the crab year.
months.markets: All markets running. Bring a cooler — a hot car in August undoes a boat's careful work in an hour.
months.cook: Coho is leaner than chinook and cooks faster. Hot and short, and take it off early.
months.buy: Coho at $18.95 against chinook at $29.95 — the same fishery and the same handling for two-thirds of the price.

months.name: September
months.headline: The best month to buy. Salmon, albacore and shrimp all at once.
months.note: Late salmon openings overlap with the albacore run and the tail of the shrimp season. More species are typically available simultaneously in September than in any other month.
months.markets: All running, with the outdoor season heading toward its close.
months.cook: The last reliably dry weeks of the year in the valley. Grill while it lasts.
months.buy: If you smoke fish at home, this is the month to buy for it — salmon and albacore both available and both ideal.

months.name: October
months.headline: The season winds down. Shrimp closes, the markets start folding.
months.note: The Oregon pink shrimp season typically closes at the end of October. Albacore taper off as the water cools. Groundfish carries the case into winter.
months.markets: Corvallis runs into late November; Bend and the Eugene Tuesday market wind down. Eugene Saturday and Portland PSU carry on year-round.
months.cook: Back indoors. Roasting and frying weather, and the start of chowder season.
months.buy: Last of the bay shrimp until April. The canned albacore is the way to keep the summer around.

months.name: November
months.headline: Groundfish takes over and the coast waits on the crab tests.
months.note: The Dungeness season is scheduled to open December 1 and in most recent years has been delayed while meat-fill and biotoxin testing is completed. November is the waiting month.
months.markets: Corvallis closes in late November. Eugene Saturday and Portland PSU continue through winter.
months.cook: The wet half of the year starts here and runs to April. Oven on.
months.buy: Black cod. It is available all year, it is the most forgiving fish in the case, and it is at its best in cold weather cooking.

months.name: December
months.headline: Crab season opens — on paper December 1, in practice usually later.
months.note: The scheduled opening is December 1, and delays are common. The season is held back until testing shows the crab have filled with meat and biotoxin levels are safe — the delay is the quality control, not a failure of it.
months.markets: Eugene Saturday and Portland PSU only. The Springfield store is open daily including through the holidays.
months.cook: Cold cracked crab with bread and butter is the traditional Oregon Christmas table and needs no improvement.
months.buy: The Smoked Seacuterie Board at $229.95 and the Brandywine Boat Gift Set at $70 are the season's gift items.
